plan.rationale: Initial plan for 4096x4096x1024 FP16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation. Chosen tiles all divide M=4096, N=4096, K=1024. Baseline swizzle=[0] as required to establish row-major reference. Shared estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) kept under 32768-byte portability cap; e.g. 128x256x32x3 gives 2*32*384*3=73728 > cap so large N with stages will be rejected by HiGHS, steering selection toward feasible combos like 64x128 and 128x128 across stages 1-3. threads=[128] single-domain baseline to isolate tile/stage effects before testing thread alternatives post-feedback. M has 4096 so many tile rows exist; reuse proxy favors larger block_M and swizzle >1, so the next round should expand swizzle [0,4,8,16,32,64] and test a changed block_K or thread domain, then retain/reject based on measured simulator traffic and latency rather than the analytic reuse hypothesis. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements.

Attempt-00 baseline selected 128x64x64,stages=1,threads=128,swizzle=0, passing numerical/SMT/compile and simulating at 470.78us with 3 blocks/SM. Shared cap 32768 implied estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N); worked well so retained. Expanded swizzle to [0,4,8,16,32,64] to test panel-reuse hypothesis since M=4096 gives many tile rows. Added block_N=256 and num_stages=4 to probe wider N and deeper pipelines (HiGHS will reject infeasible smem combos). Added threads=256 alongside 128 to test the warp-layout/thread-domain hypothesis flagged by the proxy tie, early after baseline. Dropped none since exclusion is per-tuple, not per-value. Weights kept uniform for now; will downweight analytic traffic/footprint if measured simulator traffic/latency shows reuse gains not materializing. Next hypothesis: a swizzled panel or stages=2-3 with threads=256 reduces simulated latency versus the baseline 470.78us. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements.

Attempt-01 (32x256x32,s1,t256,sw64) passed checks but regressed badly to 863.78us vs baseline 470.78us: the small block_M cut tile-row count and wide block_N plus swizzle=64 did not reduce simulated DRAM (both report 16.78MB), so the analytic panel-reuse hypothesis is unsupported so far. Revert to threads=[128], which matched the fast baseline, to isolate tile/stage/swizzle effects before re-testing warp layouts; keep the expanded swizzle and stage=4 domains to probe structural alternatives toward larger block_M/latency. block_B tiles remain under the 32768 smem cap; HiGHS excludes infeasible smem combos. Next hypothesis: larger block_M (64/128) with moderate block_N and stages=2-3 outperforms the 32-wide-M, large-N direction, since wide-M raises blocks/SM and trims redundant A traffic. Scope note: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR, GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Two failures (attempt-01 863.78us, attempt-02 679.45us) both selected block_M=32 with block_N=256 and swizzle=64; the baseline 128x64x64,s1,t128,sw0 remains best at 470.78us. Simulated DRAM stayed 16.78MB in all runs, so swizzle-driven panel reuse is not reflected in simulator traffic; analytic reuse hypothesis unsupported. Dropping block_M=32 to stop HiGHS re-picking the wide-N small-M corner, and keeping block_N=256 exploratory but hoping larger block_M wins. Reverting threads to [128] since 256 correlated with the worst result, isolating tile/stage/swizzle effects. Kept block_K [32,64], num_stages up to 4, and full swizzle set so HiGHS can still test stages=4 and moderate swizzle with wide-M tiles. Uniform weights retained because traffic proxy has not tracked latency; footprint may still matter through smem feasibility only. Next hypothesis: larger block_M (128) with moderate block_N and stages=2-3, threads=128, beats 470.78us. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Attempt-03 (64x128x64,s1,t128,sw64) edged baseline at 470.76us vs 470.78us; attempts 01-02 with block_M=32 and block_N=256 plus swizzle=64 regressed (863.78us, 679.45us). Simulated DRAM is invariant at 16.78MB across all attempts, so the analytic panel-reuse/swizzle hypothesis is unsupported by simulator traffic; we retain the full swizzle domain but expect it to be roughly neutral and rely on tile/stage effects. Drop block_M=32 (consistently slow corner) and keep threads=[128] (256 correlated with the worst run). Keep block_N=256 and num_stages=4 to probe wider-N and deeper pipelines before excluding them. Uniform weights retained since traffic proxy has not tracked latency; footprint influences feasibility only via the 32768-byte cap. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with block_N=128, stages=2-3, threads=128, swizzle in 0-16 reduces simulated latency below 470.76us by raising blocks/SM and pipelining K. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) improved best simulated latency to 462.42us vs 470.76us, confirming deeper pipelining (stages=2) helps more than swizzle, which has been latency-neutral with invariant 16.78MB DRAM across all runs; the analytic panel-reuse hypothesis remains unsupported, so I upweight pipeline (1.5) and downweight footprint (0.5) to steer HiGHS toward deeper K pipelines within the 32768 cap, while keeping traffic=1 since DRAM did not vary. Retain block_M=[64,128] (block_M=32 corner regressed twice), block_N=[64,128,256], block_K=[32,64], full swizzle, and stages up to 4 to probe pipeline depth. Changed thread domain to [64,128]: single 128 domain risked stagnation, 256 correlated with the worst run, so add 64 to test warp layout while staying on the fast side. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with stages=3-4 and threads=64/128 reduces latency below 462.42us; also test block_N=128 vs 256 at deeper stages. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Best is attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) at 462.42us. Deeper pipelining helped; swizzle has been latency-neutral with DRAM invariant at 16.78MB across all runs, so the panel-reuse hypothesis remains unsupported and weights keep traffic=1, pipeline upweighted to 1.5, footprint 0.5. Attempt-05 with threads=64 regressed to 654.98us, so revert threads to [128]; block_M=32 corner regressed twice so keep it dropped. Restrict num_stages to [2,3,4] to stop HiGHS reverting to stages=1 now that stages=2 won, and keep block_M=[64,128], block_N=[64,128,256], block_K=[32,64], full swizzle under the 32768 cap. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with stages=3-4, threads=128 reduces latency below 462.42us; also probe block_N=128 vs 64 at stage 3. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Best remains attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) at 462.42us; attempt-06 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw32) tied at 462.54us and attempt-03 (64x128x64,s1) was 470.76us, so stages=2 with block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=32 is the current sweet spot. Simulated DRAM stayed invariant at 16.78MB in every run, so the analytic panel-reuse/swizzle hypothesis is still unsupported by simulator traffic; swizzle appears latency-neutral and weights keep traffic=1, pipeline=1.5, footprint=0.5. Threads=64 regressed badly (654.98us) so it is dropped; 256 previously correlated with the worst run but that attempt confounded small block_M and wide block_N, so re-add threads=256 to retest warp layout now that the tile/stage neighborhood is pinned near the sweet spot, rather than re-spending rounds on equivalent swizzles with M-block fixed. Keep block_M=[64,128] (32 regressed twice), block_N=[64,128,256], block_K=[32,64], stages=[2,3,4] (stages=1 excluded to stop reversal), all under the 32768 cap and 32768 hard portability limit. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 or stages=3/4 combined with threads=128/256 lowers latency below 462.42us; test block_K=64 at stages=2-3 to probe deeper pipelines. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Best is attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) at 462.42us; attempt-06 (same tile, sw32) tied at 462.54us. Simulated DRAM is invariant at 16.78MB across all runs, so the analytic panel-reuse/swizzle hypothesis is unsupported by simulator traffic; swizzle looks latency-neutral and weights keep traffic=1, pipeline upweighted 1.5 (stages=2 beat stages=1), footprint 0.5. Threads=64 (654.98us) and threads=256 (474.98us) both regressed versus 128, so fix threads=[128]. block_M=32 regressed twice, keep it dropped; keep block_M=[64,128], block_N=[64,128,256], block_K=[32,64] under the 32768 cap. Prior rounds have repeatedly selected stages=2 with the same tile/stage neighborhood; to spend this round on a structural change rather than an equivalent swizzle, shift num_stages to [3,4] and confirm whether deeper pipelining at block_M=128 or block_K=64 helps. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with block_N=64/128, block_K=32/64, stages=3/4, threads=128 reduces simulated latency below 462.42us; if it regresses, deeper stages are not favored and the sweet spot is stages=2. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Best remains attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) at 462.42us; attempt-06 tied at 462.54us with sw32. Deeper stages hurt: attempt-08 (64x64x32,s3) regressed to 524.35us despite 4 blocks/SM and lower smem, so restrict num_stages to [2,3,4] but drop the block_N=64 corner that drove that pick. Threads: 64 (654.98us) and 256 (474.98us) both regressed vs 128, so fix threads=[128]; single-value domain is justified by measured feedback. Simulated DRAM invariant at 16.78MB across every run, so panel-reuse/swizzle hypothesis stays unsupported; keep traffic=1, pipeline=1.5, footprint=0.5. Narrow block_N to [128,256] to avoid slow 64-wide N, keep block_M=[64,128], block_K=[32,64], full swizzle. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with block_N=128/256 at stages=2-3, threads=128 beats 462.42us by raising tile-row count and pipelining K; if 128-wide M regresses, the 64x128x32,s2 sweet spot is confirmed locally. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Best is attempt-09 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw16) at 399.54us, a real improvement over the prior 462.42us sweet spot; it shares tile/stage/thread with attempt-04/06 (sw64/sw32 at 462.4-462.5us) so swizzle=16 is the differentiator despite invariant 16.78MB simulated DRAM — the analytic traffic feature does not capture it, so keep traffic=1, pipeline=1.5, footprint=0.5. Threads=64 (654.98us) and 256 (474.98us) regressed, so fix threads=[128]. stages=3 regressed at 64x64 (524.35us); keep num_stages=[2,3] but bias toward s2. Narrow block_N to [128] and swizzle to mid-range [8,16,32] around the winner to isolate whether sw16 or larger block_M is the driver; keep block_M=[64,128] and block_K=[32,64] to test the still-unmeasured block_M=128 / block_K=64 hypotheses. Next hypothesis: 128x128x32 or block_K=64 at stages=2 with swizzle 8-32 lowers latency below 399.54us. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
